pages.title: About me
pages.content:
Hello, and welcome to my kitchen. I am a home cook, not a chef, and that is the whole point: these recipes are written for real weeknights, small budgets and people who are learning as they go.

How I test recipes

  • Every recipe is cooked at least three times.
  • Weights and cups are both given and checked.
  • If a step can be skipped, I say so.
  • If it went wrong for me once, I tell you how to avoid it.

A few favourites to start with

  • No-knead overnight bread, for the bread-nervous.
  • Sunday lemon drizzle cake, for any day that needs it.
  • Maple pecan granola, for calmer mornings.

Cooking is not about being perfect. It is about feeding people you love, including yourself.

posts.title: Sunday lemon drizzle cake
posts.excerpt: Soft, sharp and sticky: a one-bowl loaf cake soaked in lemon syrup while it is still warm.
posts.content:
Some cakes are for celebrations. This one is for an ordinary Sunday that needs a little sunshine. It comes together in one bowl, bakes in under an hour, and the crackly sugar crust on top is the best bit.

Jump to recipe ↓

Why it works

  • Melted butter keeps the crumb tender and means no creaming.
  • Yogurt adds moisture and a gentle tang.
  • The syrup goes on while the cake is hot, so it soaks right in.

Poke more holes than you think you need. Then poke a few more.

Kitchen note

Lemon drizzle cake

  • Prep15 min
  • Bake45 min
  • Serves10 slices
  • Keeps4 days

Ingredients

  • 175 g butter, melted
  • 175 g caster sugar
  • 3 eggs
  • 150 g plain yogurt
  • Zest of 2 lemons
  • 225 g self-raising flour
  • Pinch of salt
  • For the drizzle: juice of 2 lemons and 100 g granulated sugar

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 180°C and line a loaf tin.
  2. Whisk butter, sugar, eggs, yogurt and zest in one bowl.
  3. Fold in the flour and salt until just combined.
  4. Bake for 45 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
  5. Poke holes all over, stir the drizzle and spoon it over the hot cake.
  6. Cool completely in the tin before slicing.

Use granulated sugar for the drizzle, not caster; the bigger crystals give the crunchy top.

comments.author: Rosa T.
comments.content: Made this twice this week. The second one didn't survive the evening!

comments.author: Sam W.
comments.content: Could I use oranges instead? My kids aren't keen on lemon.

posts.title: Fluffy buttermilk pancakes
posts.excerpt: Tall, tender pancakes that taste like a diner breakfast, with a trick for keeping a whole batch warm.
posts.content:
The secret to tall pancakes is not a special flour or a fancy pan. It is a thick batter, a moderate heat and a little patience before you flip.

Jump to recipe ↓

Three things to remember

  1. Do not overmix; a few lumps keep the pancakes light.
  2. Let the batter rest for five minutes while the pan heats.
  3. Flip when bubbles pop and stay open, not before.

Buttermilk pancakes

  • Prep10 min
  • Cook20 min
  • Makes12 pancakes

Ingredients

  • 250 g plain flour
  • 2 tbsp sugar
  • 1 tsp baking powder
  • ½ tsp bicarbonate of soda
  • ½ tsp salt
  • 400 ml buttermilk
  • 2 eggs
  • 40 g butter, melted

Method

  1. Whisk the dry ingredients in a large bowl.
  2. Whisk buttermilk, eggs and butter in a jug.
  3. Pour the wet into the dry and stir briefly.
  4. Cook ladlefuls in a buttered pan over medium heat, about 2 minutes a side.
  5. Keep warm in a low oven while you cook the rest.

No buttermilk? Stir a tablespoon of lemon juice into milk and wait five minutes.

comments.author: Jo P.
comments.content: The oven trick saved our Saturday breakfast. Everyone ate together for once.

posts.title: No-knead overnight bread
posts.excerpt: Four ingredients, five minutes of work and a long, lazy rise. The crust crackles as it cools.
posts.content:
If you have ever been nervous about bread, start here. Time does the kneading for you: the dough rises slowly overnight and bakes in a hot covered pot, which traps steam and gives a bakery-style crust.

Jump to recipe ↓

You need

  • A large bowl
  • A lidded casserole pot
  • Baking paper
  • A sharp knife for scoring

Timeline

  • Evening: mix (5 minutes)
  • Next morning: shape (5 minutes)
  • Bake: 45 minutes
  • Cool: 1 hour, honestly

Overnight crusty loaf

  • Prep10 min
  • Rise12–18 h
  • Bake45 min
  • Makes1 loaf

Ingredients

  • 500 g strong white flour
  • 10 g salt
  • 2 g instant yeast (½ tsp)
  • 380 ml lukewarm water

Method

  1. Mix everything into a shaggy dough, cover and leave overnight at room temperature.
  2. Tip onto a floured surface and fold into a round.
  3. Rest on baking paper for 1 hour while the pot heats in a 240°C oven.
  4. Score the top, lower it into the pot, cover and bake for 30 minutes.
  5. Uncover and bake 15 minutes more until deep golden.

Knock on the bottom of the loaf: a hollow sound means it is done.

posts.title: Rainbow chopped salad with lemon tahini
posts.excerpt: Everything chopped small, so each forkful has a bit of everything, with a creamy dressing that keeps for a week.
posts.content:
A chopped salad is the answer to a fridge full of odds and ends. Cut everything to the size of a chickpea, add something crunchy and something salty, then toss it with a dressing you will want to put on everything.

Jump to recipe ↓

Rainbow chopped salad

  • Prep20 min
  • CookNone
  • Serves4

Ingredients

  • 1 tin chickpeas, drained
  • 1 red pepper
  • ½ cucumber
  • 200 g cherry tomatoes
  • 2 carrots
  • A handful of parsley
  • 100 g feta
  • Dressing: 3 tbsp tahini, 1 lemon, 1 small garlic clove, water

Method

  1. Chop all the vegetables small and tip into a big bowl.
  2. Add the chickpeas, parsley and crumbled feta.
  3. Whisk tahini, lemon juice and grated garlic, adding water until pourable.
  4. Toss everything together just before serving.

The dressing keeps for a week in the fridge; loosen it with a splash of water.

posts.title: Roasted tomato and red pepper soup
posts.excerpt: Roasting first gives this soup a deep, sweet flavour. Freeze a batch for cold evenings.
posts.content:
Late summer tomatoes and peppers go into the oven with garlic and onions until they collapse and char at the edges. Blitzed with stock, they make a soup that tastes like it took all day.

Jump to recipe ↓

Roasted tomato soup

  • Prep15 min
  • Roast40 min
  • Serves4–6
  • Freezes3 months

Ingredients

  • 1 kg ripe tomatoes, halved
  • 2 red peppers, chunked
  • 1 red onion, quartered
  • 4 garlic cloves
  • 3 tbsp olive oil
  • 700 ml vegetable stock
  • Salt, pepper and a pinch of sugar

Method

  1. Toss the vegetables with oil and salt on a large tray.
  2. Roast at 200°C for 40 minutes, until soft and charred in places.
  3. Squeeze the garlic from its skins and tip everything into a pan with the stock.
  4. Blend until smooth, season, and simmer for 5 minutes.

A spoonful of yogurt and some toasted seeds make it feel special.

posts.title: Brown butter chocolate chip cookies
posts.excerpt: Nutty brown butter, two kinds of sugar and a rest in the fridge give chewy middles and crisp edges.
posts.content:
Browning butter takes five minutes and transforms a good cookie into a great one. The milk solids toast and smell of hazelnuts and toffee, and that flavour carries right through the dough.

Jump to recipe ↓

How to brown butter

  1. Melt the butter in a light-coloured pan so you can see it change.
  2. Keep it bubbling over medium heat, swirling often.
  3. When it smells nutty and the specks turn amber, pour it into a bowl to stop the cooking.

Brown butter cookies

  • Prep20 min
  • Chill1 h
  • Bake11 min
  • Makes16

Ingredients

  • 170 g butter
  • 150 g light brown sugar
  • 50 g caster sugar
  • 1 egg plus 1 yolk
  • 1 tsp vanilla
  • 220 g plain flour
  • ½ tsp bicarbonate of soda
  • ½ tsp salt
  • 170 g dark chocolate, chopped

Method

  1. Brown the butter and let it cool for 10 minutes.
  2. Whisk in both sugars, then the egg, yolk and vanilla.
  3. Fold in the flour, soda, salt and chocolate.
  4. Chill for at least an hour.
  5. Bake balls of dough at 180°C for 10–12 minutes; they firm up as they cool.

comments.author: Mina R.
comments.content: The flaky salt on top is non-negotiable in our house.

posts.title: Cherry lattice pie
posts.excerpt: An all-butter crust, a jammy cherry filling and a lattice that looks harder than it is.
posts.content:
A lattice top is mostly about confidence. Lay the strips, fold back every other one, add a cross strip, repeat. If it goes wrong, nobody minds: it is still pie.

Jump to recipe ↓

Cherry lattice pie

  • Prep45 min
  • Chill1 h
  • Bake55 min
  • Serves8

Ingredients

  • Pastry: 350 g plain flour, 225 g cold butter, pinch of salt, 6–8 tbsp iced water
  • 800 g pitted cherries (fresh or frozen)
  • 120 g sugar
  • 3 tbsp cornflour
  • Juice of ½ lemon
  • 1 egg, beaten, for glazing

Method

  1. Rub the butter into the flour and salt, then add water until the dough holds together. Chill.
  2. Toss the cherries with sugar, cornflour and lemon.
  3. Line a pie dish with half the pastry and fill it.
  4. Cut the rest into strips and weave a lattice over the top.
  5. Glaze and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes, then 180°C for 35 minutes, until bubbling.

Let the pie cool for three hours so the filling sets and slices cleanly.

posts.title: Rosemary and tomato focaccia
posts.excerpt: A pillowy tray bread with deep dimples, plenty of olive oil and bursting cherry tomatoes.
posts.content:
Focaccia is the friendliest bread there is. The dough is wet and sticky, there is no shaping, and pressing your fingers into it to make dimples is genuinely fun.

Jump to recipe ↓

Toppings we love

  • Cherry tomatoes and rosemary
  • Thinly sliced potato and thyme
  • Red onion and olives
  • Grapes and flaky salt

Tomato focaccia

  • Prep15 min
  • Rise2 h
  • Bake25 min
  • Serves8

Ingredients

  • 500 g strong white flour
  • 10 g salt
  • 7 g instant yeast
  • 400 ml warm water
  • 6 tbsp olive oil
  • 250 g cherry tomatoes
  • 2 sprigs rosemary
  • Flaky salt

Method

  1. Mix flour, salt, yeast and water into a sticky dough; rest 30 minutes.
  2. Fold the dough over itself a few times, then rest 1 hour.
  3. Pour half the oil into a tray, add the dough and stretch it to the corners.
  4. Rise 30 minutes, dimple deeply, add tomatoes, rosemary and the rest of the oil.
  5. Bake at 220°C for 25 minutes.

posts.title: Maple pecan granola
posts.excerpt: Big clusters, toasted pecans and just enough maple. Make a jar on Sunday and breakfast is sorted.
posts.content:
Shop-bought granola is often too sweet and never clustery enough. Homemade takes five minutes to mix, and the secret to clusters is simple: press it flat and do not stir it while it bakes.

Jump to recipe ↓
  • Stores for two weeks in an airtight jar.
  • Swap pecans for any nut or seed.
  • Add dried fruit after baking, never before.

Maple pecan granola

  • Prep5 min
  • Bake30 min
  • Makes1 big jar

Ingredients

  • 300 g rolled oats
  • 120 g pecans, roughly chopped
  • 50 g pumpkin seeds
  • ½ tsp cinnamon
  • Pinch of salt
  • 90 ml maple syrup
  • 60 ml olive or coconut oil
  • 1 egg white (optional, for clusters)

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 160°C and line a tray.
  2. Mix everything in one bowl until evenly coated.
  3. Press firmly into a flat layer.
  4. Bake for 30 minutes, turning the tray once but not stirring.
  5. Cool completely, then break into clusters.

The egg white is the cluster secret. Whisk it until frothy before adding.
